notices.title: Correction to historical quality guidance
paragraphs: The preserved lesson below includes outdated quality claims. Scores can be missing or Unscored; neither establishes a pass or failure. A score describes the tested cases and configuration, not the correctness of the current answer.
Additional test cases can expose failures and lower a score. Saving a test case does not itself repair an artifact. Check source values and inspect measured reruns before claiming improvement.
Chat can receive score metadata. Inspect the stored evaluation details rather than relying on an assurance. Successful execution and reviewer acceptance are separate from measured correctness.

notices.title: Correction to historical arithmetic guidance
paragraphs: Deep Analysis uses model-based analysis and synthesis. It can interpret a budget, but it is not a deterministic calculator and cannot establish that totals are correct merely by saying it checked them.

Check the source amounts and units, state the formula, and preserve a calculator result or explicitly recorded human arithmetic. Authorized code is another option where available; elevated access is not required for the separate calculation route.

Compare the actual model output with that calculation. A memo that depends on the check must wait for its result. Correct addition alone cannot resolve a missing amount, wrong input or unclear cost category.

notices.title: Correction to historical course and control guidance
paragraphs: Completing Governance alone or reading its closing lesson does not issue the credential. Every required module must satisfy its preserved course rules; saved progress and the issued certificate establish actual completion. A credential does not guarantee future outputs or grant institutional approval authority.

The course is self-paced. Earlier fixed module durations, rapid-review targets and promised time savings were not established by measured learner performance. Allow time for source checks, repairs and assessed work.

Inspect the actual saved workflow, selected inputs and step or task input settings. A chat proposal does not prove the right configuration was saved. Place a required approval before its dependent action, and inspect reviewer and timeout behavior; a written instruction alone is not a runtime pause.

Use the supported Include in deliverables download path for multiple outputs and inspect the resulting ZIP members. No future Package Builder node is promised. Inspect export contents and portability warnings, resolve permitted local dependencies after import and test the imported revision. Review status and measured validation are separate evidence.

notices.title: Current guidance on extraction settings and source checks
paragraphs: Optional fields, Allowed values and structured output control permitted absence or output shape. They do not establish that an answer is supported by the source. A required field can remain missing, an allowed category can be wrong, and an optional field can still contain an invented value. Missing evidence is not automatically No.

Two-pass extraction attempts a draft and refinement, with separately configurable models and reasoning settings. Refinement can retain or introduce an error, and refinement failure can return the first-pass draft. A completed result does not prove two successful independent checks.

Consensus starts with two attempts and can add another when their answers disagree. Agreement is consistency, not proof of truth. Calls and usage also depend on passes, field grouping and failure handling; there is no guaranteed three-call or three-times-cost rule, or guaranteed highest accuracy.

Field grouping depends on enabled chunking and its configured group size; a list exceeding 20 fields does not automatically activate it. Inspect the saved settings and compare actual results with representative sources.

Treat the original worked repair as an illustration, not an executed result or guarantee. Establish a repair by inspecting the saved revision, running that revision on the intended source and checking the new amount, period, unit and other required values. Retain unresolved evidence instead of claiming success.

notices.title: Current guidance on connected inputs and supported conclusions
paragraphs: A step receives its configured sources, which may include the preceding output, workflow documents or a selected document. Tasks normally use the step input but can have an explicit override. Inspect the saved settings and actual intermediate results rather than assuming every step sees only its predecessor or all workspace documents.

Extraction is useful when fixed fields preserve the context needed downstream; it is not required before every Prompt. More steps do not guarantee better answers. A written reviewer checkpoint does not itself pause execution; configure and test the actual approval boundary when an action must wait.

The original worked chain is illustrative, not evidence of your assigned run. Its example amount and precise reporting date are not answer keys for the assigned subaward. Check the assigned source and required budget scope. Reporting frequency alone may not establish the first due date; comparison with an institutional standard requires the actual reference rule.

Prompt, Formatter and post-process instructions can introduce unsupported claims or remove uncertainty. Check each saved result against its inputs and source. Preserve failed history and successful outputs before recovery; a canceled or lost chat reply does not undo executed work.

notices.title: Current guidance on batch coverage and targeted recovery
paragraphs: Batch mode queues one workflow execution per selected document; workers need not finish in selection order. Inspect per-document results and reconcile the actual inputs. An aggregate Completed label can coexist with failed items, and completed processing does not prove correct values.

A basic pilot is useful but one easy document does not establish accuracy across a varied collection. Inspect effective models and overrides, source-supported values and measured usage. Batch mode does not guarantee that a validation plan ran or automatically merge every output into a correct dataset.

For an unreadable scan, inspect the text actually available, repair the permitted source or ingestion and check the repaired text before a new run. Re-uploading identical poor bytes is not a guaranteed repair. Preserve successful results and the original failure, select only the justified retry input, and verify any already-executed external action before repeating it.

A batch download can omit failed or unfinished items. Inspect its actual members and retain an exception list. A small random spot check and a plausible result do not prove every output is correct; source-check the values required for the task. The thirty-proposal story is illustrative, not an executed result.

notices.title: Current guidance on generated files and release scope
paragraphs: File generation does not establish correctness or permission to share. Identify the intended recipient and data scope, inspect the actual file, and preserve unresolved content. A download-only exercise does not authorize sending files externally.

An output task receives its configured input. Data Export needs suitable tabular input for CSV; a narrative paragraph does not automatically preserve the original rows, and sibling tasks do not get different sources just because their formats differ. Inspect saved source settings, actual output format and warnings.

The original two-deliverable story is illustrative. Its publication count, delay and spending percentage are not verified answer keys. Preserve reviewed rows for the data export and supply the intended source for the narrative, then compare both actual files with the assigned report. Include in deliverables can bundle marked outputs; inspect every ZIP member rather than assuming one download contains complete, usable and authorized files.

notices.title: Current guidance on sharing receipts and imported workflows
paragraphs: A sharing request and an imported file are separate from an assessed course completion. Use the course check and completion actions to establish saved credit under your existing requirements. Examiner review remains a separate product process; it is not a routine certification grading queue.

Inspect a workflow export before sharing it: it can contain prompts, extraction definitions, text validation inputs and exporter metadata. Confirm the intended audience and data scope. Export/import does not automatically carry every source, access right, configured model or integration.

Inspect portability warnings and the imported tasks, resolve authorized local references, and test the imported revision. Keep the tested original and imported/adapted revisions distinguishable. Record actual sharing and validation evidence; successful import alone does not establish readiness or make the original score current.

module_notices.title: Current guidance on earning the credential
paragraphs: Completing Governance alone does not issue the Vandal Workflow Architect credential. Every required module must satisfy its original course rules. Use your saved course progress and issued certificate to establish actual completion; reading this module is not a completion receipt.

module_notices.title: Current guidance on course pace
paragraphs: This course is self-paced. Fixed module times in the original description were not established by measured learner performance. Allow time for reading, source checking, repairs and assessed work, and return to your saved reading place when needed.

module_notices.title: Known limitation in historical star guidance
paragraphs: The original three-star description says four task types, but this course version’s saved grading rule requires at least five task types and counts them across the learner’s workflows. The description and grading rule therefore disagree. Those historical counts do not establish one correctly executed workflow or a verified output.

Do not add unrelated tasks or unnecessary steps simply to pursue an optional star. This notice does not introduce a replacement grading rule, award stars or change required module completion. Existing requirements and earned credit remain preserved. A supported equivalent assessment still requires a separately reviewed course amendment or optional new course release.
